quote: you guys represent you guys represent the Tesla ones as well?
stewart_read: Customer is probing whether Ion sells Tesla-branded black panels specifically. Rep never clarifies Ion sells its own panels, not Tesla panels/tiles.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have judged this a minor aside not worth interrupting rapport-building for at the setter stage.
coaching_implication: This is exactly the tesla_expectation_gap pattern — customer's whole motivation ('black solar paneling') may hinge on a Tesla product Ion doesn't sell. Should be flagged for the closer if not clarified now.

quote: What would it cost to put in black solar paneling?
stewart_read: Customer is highly engaged, connecting a home renovation (painting the house black) to solar aesthetics — a strong buying signal tied to a specific want (black panels).
coaching_implication: Rep should have used this as the emotional anchor for the appointment ('the design team can show you what black panels look like on your roof') rather than letting it pass into the next verify question.

stewart_read: Bill pain is stated directly and unprompted ('too much') — a ready-made emotional hook the rep only partially used.
coaching_implication: Rep acknowledged the bill ('that's a lot') but never flipped it into 'that $300 becomes your reason to see this design' — capture without flip.

quote: What I can do, if it's easier for you,
stewart_read: Rep swaps a live capture attempt for a text/email follow-up, correctly avoiding burning call time on a slow tech path.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read: rep gave up too early on live capture. Strategic read is stronger — call is inbound/short and rep prioritizes locking the appointment.
coaching_implication: Good instinct on pacing, but rep should explicitly tie the callback slot to receiving that document first so the specialist isn't walking in blind.

quote: Doesn't seem to be really any shading along that roof.
stewart_read: Roof qualifier is stated by the rep as an observation rather than asked as a question, and the customer never confirms roof type/age — verified events mark this 'partial' and 'moved_on'.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have pulled satellite imagery and considered it self-evident, deciding not to press further.
coaching_implication: Roof age/type should still be confirmed verbally per verify.roof_type_age — an assumed-from-imagery roof read isn't the same as customer confirmation.

quote: Oh, jeez. Yeah. That's a lot to be paying for electricity.
stewart_read: This is the acknowledge step of ask+acknowledge+flip — the flip into urgency/against-utility framing never comes.
coaching_implication: A one-line flip ('that $300 a month is basically what you'd be putting toward owning the system instead') was available and unused.
